Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

before the sheets are filed compare the cooler figures with the handwritten tray labels and write the count time beside the temperature reading if the kitchen log confirms the carrots were prepared today they can be counted on a separate prepared food line rather than added to the raw produce total the annex flour count is forty eight sealed bags plus one opened bag with about seven pounds remaining and the open bag is clipped shut on the lower pallet the front door key is back on its hook and the blue board still has the previous week's sheet underneath the new one leave both sheets there until the manager signs the weekly review line on friday", "output": "We are reviewing the Harbor Table food cooperative inventory for the week ending October seventeenth, and this is the count from the main room, the annex pantry, and the walk-in cooler. The main room has the public shelves and the dry goods rack, while the annex holds bulk flour, jars, and the boxes set aside for the Friday neighborhood pickup. We counted after closing on Thursday with two volunteers and one staff member, and the paper count sheets are clipped to the blue board beside the office door. The register totals are not part of this count because those are checked separately at the end of each month.

For dry goods, we checked the lot label as well as the package count because several donations arrived with mixed dates. The brown rice shelf has thirty-six bags in sealed cases and five loose bags with a torn outer sack but intact inner packages. The oat bin is about two-thirds full, and the scoop was left in a clean container instead of inside the bin. We have fourteen jars of tomato sauce with lids that are slightly dented but still sealed, and there are no swollen cans on the lower rack. The lentils in the annex came in two different bag sizes, so the sheet records them as twenty-one large bags and twelve small bags rather than using a single weight estimate.

Mara is the receiving lead, and she checked the boxes against the donation slips before they were moved into storage. She noted that three crates of apples were marked Gala on the slip, but the fruit inside was mostly Honeycrisp, so she left the variety field blank for now and asked Joel to confirm the farm label on the next delivery. The apples are in the ventilated crate under the north window and should not be mixed with the older pears because those have soft spots on several pieces. The pears are still suitable for cooking, and the kitchen team has reserved them for sauce on Monday.

In the cooler, we counted two trays of eggs with thirty eggs in each tray and a partly used tray with eleven eggs. The milk shelf has nine cartons dated October nineteenth and six dated October twenty-first, and the oat milk cartons are on the separate lower shelf because the label says, “Keep chilled after opening.” We have four tubs of plain yogurt for the cooking class and three tubs for the member shelf. There is also a covered pan of chopped carrots from the community meal, but it has no date sticker, so do not include it in the available produce total until someone checks the kitchen log. The temperature reading at the end of the count was thirty-eight degrees, and the probe was wiped before it went back in its case.

1. Record the dry beans by type and package size.
2. Put the five rice bags from the torn outer sack on the shelf marked “Inspect before distribution,” and keep their inner packages sealed.
3. Move the dented but sealed sauce jars to the front row so the next checker can see them without treating them as damaged goods.
4. Ask Joel to confirm the apple variety and add it to the sheet only after he checks the farm label.
5. Leave the carrots off the available produce total until the date is verified.

These steps are written on the task card, and the volunteers initial each one when it is complete. The last initial is still blank because Joel has not returned from the annex yet.

We use the same count sheet for the Saturday pickup, but the reserve column is only for food that has been promised to a household or a class. The six cartons of milk dated October twenty-first are not reserved and can stay in general stock. The yogurt for the cooking class is reserved and should not be moved to the member shelf unless the instructor cancels the class. If the cooler reading rises above forty-one degrees at any point before opening, then the dairy cartons and yogurt need to be held apart from general stock while the manager checks the temperature log and decides whether they can be distributed. The condition matters because the cooler door did not close easily last week, and the maintenance visit is booked for Tuesday.

At the morning handoff, Priya said the volunteers should use the green stickers for items that need a second look and the white stickers for ordinary shelf counts. Joel said the sign on the annex door reads, “Keep the flour pallet clear,” because the building inspector needs access to the drain, and nobody should stack donation boxes in that marked area. The flour is on two low pallets beside the wall, and there is a clear path from the door to the drain. The paper towels are nearly gone, so Priya added them to the supply list but did not count them as food inventory. She also asked whether the extra apple crates could go to the pickup table, and the group agreed to wait for the variety check first.

Before the sheets are filed, compare the cooler figures with the handwritten tray labels and write the count time beside the temperature reading. If the kitchen log confirms the carrots were prepared today, they can be counted on a separate prepared food line rather than added to the raw produce total. The annex flour count is forty-eight sealed bags plus one opened bag with about seven pounds remaining, and the open bag is clipped shut on the lower pallet. The front door key is back on its hook, and the blue board still has the previous week's sheet underneath the new one. Leave both sheets there until the manager signs the weekly review line on Friday."}]
